Here’s a quick reference for the **long‑weekend holidays in Canada for 2023** (i.e., holidays that fall on a weekday and create a three‑day weekend).  
(If a holiday falls on a weekend, the “observed” day is usually the following Monday.)

| Holiday | 2023 Date | Observed (if applicable) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-----------|--------------------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Jan 2 (Monday) | Jan 1 – 3 |
| Family Day (Ontario, Alberta, Saskatchewan, etc.) | Feb 20 (Monday) | — | Feb 18 – 20 |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | — | Apr 7 – 10 |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | — | May 20 – 22 |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Jul 3 (Monday) | Jul 1 – 3 |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | — | Sep 2 – 4 |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 (Monday) | — | Oct 7 – 9 |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 (Friday) | Nov 13 (Monday) | Nov 11 – 13 |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Monday) | — | Dec 23 – 25 |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 (Tuesday) | — | Dec 24 – 26 |

> **Quick Tips for Your App**  
> • Use the “Observed” column to adjust the holiday date if it falls on a weekend.  
> • For province‑specific holidays (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Ontario, St. George’s Day in British Columbia), add separate entries as needed.  
> • Store the long‑weekend spans as date ranges so users can filter or highlight them in your UI.  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like province‑specific lists or additional details!
